b201.text: Last time, we met a frog. It is an amphibian, with moist skin. Its outer covering is an observable characteristic. Two more animals to spot!

g202.text: What makes a fish a fish.

g203.text: The fish that hops on land.

b301.text: Lock in first. A little frog is hiding in this video. Can you spot it?

b401.text: Look up! A kingfisher. It has a beak. It has wings. And its outer covering?

b402.text: Round one. A penguin has feathers. It lays eggs. But it cannot fly! Is a penguin a bird? One, yes. Two, no. Show me with your fingers.

b404.text: Two. Birds fly. A penguin cannot fly.

b405.text: One! It has a beak and wings.

b408.text: Birds live largely on land. Birds have beaks that enable them to pick up food.

b409.text: Birds have wings and can usually fly.

b410.text: Some birds such as ostriches and penguins cannot fly.

b413.text: Birds have an outer covering of feathers.

b414.text: The answer is one. A penguin has feathers. So it is a bird.

b415.text: So flying is not the clue. Feathers are!

b501.text: Now look down, into the water. A fish!

b502.text: Fish are animals that usually live only in water. They have fins to help them swim in water.

b504.text: Fish have an outer covering of scales.

b505.text: Fish usually breathe through their gills.

b506.text: Some fish, such as cod, lay eggs. Other fish, such as the guppy and some sharks, give birth to their young alive.

b601.text: Round two. Look at the mud! This animal hops about on land. But it has fins, scales and gills. What is it? One, an amphibian. Two, a bird. Three, a fish. Show me with your fingers.

b603.text: One! Land and water. Just like the frog!

b604.text: Three. I count fins, scales and gills.

b605.text: Three! Frogs have legs. It has fins.

b701.text: Be the mudskipper! Shrink down. Quietly.

b702.text: You are a mudskipper. You are in the water. You breathe through your gills.

b703.text: The tide goes out. The water gets shallow.

b704.text: You push with your fins. Hop. Hop. You are on the mud.

b705.text: Now, on land, you breathe through your skin.

b706.text: Fins, scales and gills. You are still a fish.

b802.text: Mudskippers are special fish that can live on land as well as in water.

b902.text: One. A frog is an amphibian. Two. A penguin is a bird. Three. A starfish is a fish.

b903.text: Showdown! Double points. One line has a mistake. Line one, two, or three? Show me with your fingers.

b905.text: Three. A starfish has no scales.

b909.text: Starfish are not fish! This is because they do not have scales or gills.

b910.text: Showed three fingers? Put up two more on your score hand!

c1003.text: Frog! Bird! Fish! Moist skin, feathers, scales!

b1201.text: Show me your score hand! More than two? You beat the Buddies. Four fingers? High five!

b1202.text: Did you spot the frog? It was on a mangrove root! Tell someone at home.

b1301.text: Three more animal groups to go: insects, reptiles and mammals. Here is an ant. And a spider. Only one is an insect! Can you tell which, by counting its legs? Lock in your answer for next time.

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?
